# English grammar fixture for the built-in rules (competitiveness plan 6.1/6.5).
#
# One sentence per line. An error is written [[flagged text|rule_id]]: the flagged text is exactly the
# range the rule should report. A line with no markers is a clean sentence: any finding on it is a
# false positive. Lines that begin with # are comments. The labels follow the grammar, not the rules'
# behaviour, so errors the rules cannot see are included and show up as missed (recall below 1.0).
# Dialect and dialogue lines are marked "(dialogue)" in comments only; the rules decide for themselves.

# --- confusion: modal of ----------------------------------------------------------------------
I should [[of|modal_of]] told you about the meeting.
She could [[of|modal_of]] gone to the party if she had wanted to.
They would [[of|modal_of]] won the game with a better coach.
We must [[of|modal_of]] left the keys in the car.
He might [[of|modal_of]] forgotten the appointment entirely.
It was a decision that would of course change everything.
I could have been there earlier if the train had run on time.
You should have called me before you left.

# --- confusion: its / it's ---------------------------------------------------------------------
[[Its|its_for_its_contraction]] a long way to the coast from here.
I think [[its|its_for_its_contraction]] going to rain this afternoon.
The dog wagged its tail and ran to the door.
The company announced its plans for next year.
[[Its|its_for_its_contraction]] been three years since we last spoke.
I believe [[its|its_for_its_contraction]] the right choice for the team.
The committee said its time had come to act.
The tree lost its leaves in October.
She noticed that [[it's|contraction_for_its]] own shadow had grown longer.
It's a beautiful morning and the garden is quiet.
It's been a long week, and I am ready to rest.
Its meaning was clear to everyone in the room.
The cat licked its paws and settled in the sun.

# --- confusion: your / you're ------------------------------------------------------------------
[[Your|your_for_youre]] welcome to stay as long as you like.
I hope [[your|your_for_youre]] not angry with me about yesterday.
Tell me when [[your|your_for_youre]] ready to leave.
I think [[your|your_for_youre]] the best person for the job.
Your welcome speech was warm and funny.
Your brother called while you were out.
You're welcome to stay as long as you like.
I know you're tired, but we have to keep going.
Please write [[you're|youre_for_your]] name at the top of the page.
Is that [[you're|youre_for_your]] own handwriting on the note?
Your own handwriting is better than mine.
Your account has been updated and your password has changed.

# --- confusion: there / their / they're --------------------------------------------------------
[[Their|their_for_there]] is a problem with the printer on the second floor.
I think [[their|their_for_there]] are three of us who can come.
[[Their|their_for_there]] was nothing left to say after that.
They forgot to bring [[there|there_for_their]] own lunch to the trip.
The kids said [[they're|theyre_for_their]] own parents would drive them home.
Their house sits at the end of the lane.
There is a problem with the printer on the second floor.
They finished their homework before dinner.
There was nothing left to say after that.
[[Their|?confusion]] going to be late for the train again.

# --- confusion: then / than; to / too ------------------------------------------------------------
She is taller [[then|then_for_than]] her brother by almost two inches.
It was better [[then|then_for_than]] anything I had hoped for.
It was bigger [[then|then_for_than]] the house we saw in May.
We finished the soup and then we ordered dessert.
It is more expensive than the one we saw yesterday.
He opened the door, and then he stepped outside.
She was older then, and wiser than she had ever been.
We ate first and [[than|than_for_then]] we cleaned the kitchen.
I want [[too|to_for_too_verb]] go home before it gets dark.
They need [[too|to_for_too_verb]] be more careful with the budget.
It is [[to|too_for_to]] much to ask of anyone at this hour.
It was [[to|too_for_to]] late to call anyone by then.
I have too many books and not enough shelves.
She went to the market to buy bread.
It is too late to start again today.
He was going too fast on the wet road.

# --- confusion: lose / loose; whose / who's ----------------------------------------------------------
Don't [[loose|loose_for_lose]] your keys on the way home.
I am afraid we will [[loose|loose_for_lose]] track of the time again.
The screw came loose and rattled across the floor.
She wore a loose shirt and old sandals.
Make sure you do not lose your ticket.
He bought a [[lose|lose_for_loose]] fitting jacket for the trip.
[[Who's|whos_for_whose]] car is parked across my driveway?
I wonder [[who's|whos_for_whose]] idea this was in the first place.
Who's coming to dinner on Friday?
Whose coat is this on the chair?
I met a woman [[whose|whose_for_whos]] been to every continent.
Do you know [[whose|whose_for_whos]] going to the airport tonight?
I know a man whose daughter plays the cello.

# --- confusion: affect / effect; weather / whether; led; advice; breath ----------------------------
The new law will have a big [[affect|affect_for_effect]] on small farms.
The noise had a negative [[affect|affect_for_effect]] on the neighbours.
The storm may [[effect|effect_for_affect]] our travel plans on Monday.
Rain can affect the way a surface wears over time.
The effect of the medicine wore off after an hour.
We have not decided [[weather|weather_for_whether]] or not to go.
The [[whether|whether_for_weather]] was cold and wet all week.
Whether or not we go depends on the weather.
The captain was [[lead|lead_for_led]] by his scouts through the marsh.
She had [[lead|lead_for_led]] the team for six years before she retired.
The pipes were made of lead and had to be replaced.
Her wise leadership has led the town through hard times.
I would [[advice|advice_for_advise]] you to wait until morning.
She gave me some good [[advise|advise_for_advice]] about the contract.
He offered some advice and then he left.
He tried to [[breath|breath_for_breathe]] slowly and calm his heart.
She took a deep [[breathe|breathe_for_breath]] before opening the letter.
He drew a deep breath and began to speak.
Please bear with me while I find the file.
Please [[bare|bare_for_bear]] with me while I find the file.
He jumped [[of|of_for_off]] the wall and landed in the grass.
It [[maybe|maybe_for_may_be]] true, but I have no proof of it.
Maybe we should try the other road.

# --- agreement ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
He [[don't|third_person_dont]] like cold coffee in the morning.
She [[don't|third_person_dont]] want to talk about it anymore.
It [[don't|third_person_dont]] matter what they say.
He doesn't like cold coffee in the morning.
Why don't you come with us tomorrow?
"I don't know," he said, "and he don't either."
He said it was late, and he [[have|third_person_have]] no wish to stay.
She [[have|third_person_have]] a gift for making people laugh.
Does he have a spare key for the back door?
Would she have said yes if you had asked her?
They [[was|plural_was]] late for the meeting again.
We [[was|plural_was]] tired after the long drive home.
You [[was|plural_was]] right about the weather yesterday.
They were late for the meeting again.
We were tired after the long drive home.
They [[has|plural_pronoun_has]] finished the whole report already.
We [[has|plural_pronoun_has]] plenty of time before the train.
They [[is|plural_pronoun_is]] still working on the engine.
You [[is|plural_pronoun_is]] welcome to join us later.
I [[is|first_person_is_are]] ready to begin the lesson now.
I [[are|first_person_is_are]] not certain about the date.
I [[has|first_person_has]] a question about the schedule.
The letter I is the ninth in the alphabet.
It [[are|third_person_are]] too heavy to carry upstairs alone.
Everyone [[are|everyone_are]] welcome at the open house.
Nobody [[are|everyone_are]] ready for the surprise yet.
Everyone is welcome at the open house.
There [[is|there_is_plural]] many reasons to visit in the spring.
There [[was|there_is_plural]] several people waiting outside the gate.
There are many reasons to visit in the spring.
There is a reason for everything he does.
There was a lot of noise from the street.

# --- verb forms -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
She should have [[went|participle_after_have]] to the doctor sooner.
They would have [[ate|participle_after_have]] the whole cake if we had let them.
He might have [[wrote|participle_after_have]] the letter before he left.
I could have [[did|participle_after_have]] it myself in an hour.
She should have gone to the doctor sooner.
They would have eaten the whole cake if we had let them.
I have [[went|participle_after_have]] to that shop many times.
She has [[came|participle_after_have]] every day this week.
They had [[took|participle_after_have]] the wrong road in the dark.
We have [[saw|participle_after_have]] the film twice already.
He had [[wore|participle_after_have]] the same coat for ten winters.
I have seen the film twice already.
He had worn the same coat for ten winters.
I [[seen|simple_past_for_participle]] him leave the building around noon.
We [[done|simple_past_for_participle]] the whole job before lunch.
Have you seen the new gallery on Fifth Street?
I have done everything you asked me to do.
Did you see the rainbow after the storm?
They didn't [[used|didnt_used_to]] to live this close to the sea.
He didn't use to like olives.
You are [[suppose|suppose_to]] to sign here and here.
I was [[use|use_to_participle]] to the quiet of the village by then.
She said he [[can't|cant_hardly]] hardly wait for the holiday.
I don't have [[no|double_negative_no]] money for the bus today.
She didn't have any money for the bus today.
He can hardly wait for the holiday.

# --- pronoun case -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This is just between you and [[I|between_you_and_i]], so please keep it quiet.
They sent a gift to you and [[I|between_you_and_i]] after the wedding.
[[Me and him|object_pronoun_subject]] went to the lake after school.
[[Her and me|object_pronoun_subject]] were friends for years.
This is just between you and me, so please keep it quiet.
She and I went to the lake after school.
He gave the keys to Maria and me before he left.
You and I should talk about the plan.
The teacher spoke with him and her about the project.

# --- quantity -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
There were [[less|less_for_fewer]] people at the concert than last year.
We have [[less|less_for_fewer]] books than guests for the dinner.
She made [[less|less_for_fewer]] mistakes on the second test.
There were fewer people at the concert than last year.
We have less time than we thought we had.
He drinks less coffee than he used to.
There is [[fewer|fewer_for_less]] water in the lake than there was in May.
We need [[fewer|fewer_for_less]] noise in the library, please.
The recipe uses fewer eggs and less butter.
The [[amount|amount_for_number]] of people in the room surprised everyone.
A large [[amount|amount_for_number]] of students asked about the exam.
A large amount of money was spent on the repairs.
The number of people in the room surprised everyone.
Too [[much|much_for_many]] people were talking at once to hear the speaker.
He doesn't have [[much|much_for_many]] friends in the new town.
She did not make many friends in the new town.
There is too much noise in the street to sleep.
Too [[many|many_for_much]] information was crammed onto the slide.
She gave me [[many|many_for_much]] advice, and I ignored it.
We have many options for the evening.
Many software engineers work from home on Fridays.
There were fewer water bottles on the shelf than yesterday.

# --- punctuation ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The roads were icy[[,|comma_splice_adverb]] however the buses ran on time all day.
We ran out of paper[[,|comma_splice_adverb]] therefore we had to print the rest tomorrow.
The roads were icy; however, the buses ran on time all day.
The roads were icy, but the buses ran on time all day.
It rained all day, however hard we hoped for sun.
The report was late; [[however|semicolon_adverb_comma]] we still read it carefully.
The plan is simple; moreover, it costs very little.
He was tall[[,|comma_splice_clauses]] she was short, and nobody minded.
She smiled[[,|comma_splice_clauses]] he nodded at her across the table.
He came, he saw, he conquered.
When she arrived, she took off her coat.
She was tired, so she went to bed early.
I know that [[i|lowercase_i]] was wrong about the date.
We left early because [[i|lowercase_i]] had a headache.
I think we can be there by nine, and I will bring the maps.
The list has items i, ii and iii.

# --- idioms and misused phrases --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I [[could care less|could_care_less]] about the ranking.
I couldn't care less about the ranking.
[[For all intensive purposes|intensive_purposes]], the project is finished.
We need to nip it in the [[butt|nip_in_the_butt]] before the rumour spreads.
The storm will [[wreck|wreck_havoc]] havoc on the coast tonight.
The storm will wreak havoc on the coast tonight.
The heir was given free [[reign|free_reign]] over the estate accounts.
The story [[peaked|peak_interest]] my interest from the first page.
The crowd waited with [[baited|baited_breath]] breath for the announcement.
The plan is not, per [[say|per_say]], a bad one.
They made him the [[escape goat|escape_goat]] for the failure.
It's a [[doggy dog world|doggy_dog]] out there for a new writer.
His remark was meant [[tongue and cheek|tongue_and_cheek]] and nobody took offence.
She and her sister are [[one in the same|one_in_the_same]] when it comes to cooking.
That is a [[mute point|mute_point]] now that the vote is over.
Here is a sneak [[peak|sneak_peak]] of the new cover.
Don't take it for [[granite|for_granite]] that the road is open.
He [[wet|wet_appetite]] your appetite with a story about the harvest.
We will have to make [[due|make_due]] with what we have.
By [[in|by_in_large]] large, the readers liked the ending.
All of [[the|all_of_the_sudden]] sudden, the lights went out.
It was [[irregardless|irregardless]] of the cost.
The tent was [[pacifically|pacifically]] designed for hikers.
[[Were|were_for_where]] is the nearest station?
[[Supposably|supposably]] the train leaves at six.
It was a case [[and|case_and_point]] point of bad timing.
We decided on a [[coarse|coarse_of_action]] of action by Friday.
He refused to [[tow|tow_the_line]] the line.
We bought pens, paper, [[and |and_etc]]etc.
The sail had a coarse weave and a salt-stiff edge.
In due course the letters were delivered.
We waited with bated breath for the announcement.
She toes the line when the manager is in the room.

# --- usage ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I like it [[alot|run_together_words]] more than the old one.
She waits for the bus [[everytime|run_together_words]] it rains.
They went to the shop [[aswell|run_together_words]] to pick up the paper.
[[Noone|run_together_words]] knew where the keys had gone.
I [[dont|missing_apostrophe]] know where the station is.
She [[cant|missing_apostrophe]] come to the meeting on Thursday.
I think [[thats|missing_apostrophe]] the best idea so far.
They [[werent|missing_apostrophe]] home when I called.
We lost a lot of time on the road.
Everyone went home early, and no one stayed to clean up.
In case of rain, the picnic moves indoors.
I don't know where the station is.

# --- known gaps: real errors the rules do not catch (they count against recall) -----------------------
She [[lays|?confusion]] down for a nap every afternoon.
The puppy dragged [[it's|?confusion]] favourite toy across the floor.
I think [[your|?confusion]] right about the date.
[[There|?confusion]] best friend is waiting at the gate.
She had [[swore|?verb_form]] never to return to the city.
It was a secret between [[he|?pronoun_case]] and me.
[[Him|?pronoun_case]] and the others left before the end.
[[Less|?quantity]] cookies were left after the party.
I wanted to go[[,|?punctuation]] I was too tired to move.
He got away [[scotch free|?idiom]] after the trial.
[[Ive|?usage]] been there twice this year.

# --- clean prose: sentences that must produce no findings ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The morning light fell across the kitchen table and warmed the cold tea.
Marta folded the map and slipped it into the pocket of her coat.
"Where are you going?" he asked, and she did not answer him.
The village lay quiet under the snow, and no smoke rose from the chimneys.
He had not slept well, and the long road ahead did nothing to help.
If I were you, I would wait until the weather clears.
It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
Neither of the sisters wanted to speak first.
The committee has made its decision and will publish it on Monday.
Whoever finds the key should return it to the front desk.
They each have a copy of the report, so there is no need to share.
The children were playing in the garden while their parents cooked.
Between the two of us, we can finish the job by noon.
She asked him to bring the files, but he forgot them at home.
The results, which were published last week, surprised the researchers.
After the storm passed, we walked down to the harbour to see the damage.
He said that his name was Tom and that he had come from the north.
Each of the players was given a medal at the end of the season.
The old house on the hill has stood empty for more than a decade.
We were hoping to arrive before dark, but the roads were closed.
There was a time when the river ran clear all the way to the sea.
The best part of the trip was the night we spent in the mountains.
You are the only person who knows where the letters are hidden.
I wish he were here to see how the garden has grown.
She has been writing every morning since she moved to the coast.
The team wants to know whether the budget will cover the extra week.
What the critics missed was how quietly the film ended.
He walked slowly, listening to the river, and thought about nothing at all.
The train was late, so we missed the first act of the play.
Only a few of the guests had read the book before the party.
The weather turned cold, and we lit the stove for the first time that year.
It is not clear who wrote the letter or why it was never sent.
The two friends made a pact never to speak of that summer again.
In the end, the answer was simpler than any of us had guessed.
He read the note twice and then folded it into his pocket.
They have lived there for years, yet they know almost nobody in town.
Seven people applied for the job, and three of them were interviewed.
The garden needs less water in winter than in summer.
Fewer than half of the seats were taken when the curtain rose.
The number of visitors has doubled since the new road opened.
She took the longer route because it was safer than the cliff path.
Do you know whose turn it is to wash the dishes?
The price of bread went up, but nobody complained.
